Summary of implemented functionality: Added auth.proto and event.proto, buf configuration and scripts/proto-gen.sh with a --check drift mode.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: New build-time requirement: buf, protoc-gen-go and protoc-gen-go-grpc are needed to regenerate; check.sh now fails on stale generated code.
Deviations & technical decisions: Separate proto packages (sela.auth.v1, sela.event.v1) share one directory, so buf lint exceptions PACKAGE_DIRECTORY_MATCH and DIRECTORY_SAME_PACKAGE were added. event.proto is contract only. CreateEventRequest has no host_id: ownership comes from the session.

Summary of implemented functionality: Moved all Go backend code under apps/api and moved go.mod there with the module path unchanged.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: STRUCTURAL: cmd/, internal/ and go.mod moved to apps/api; the db package became internal/db (import path github.com/Briyantama/SELA/internal/db). Go commands must now run from apps/api; scripts/check.sh updated.
Deviations & technical decisions: Migrations live inside internal/db because Go embed cannot reference parent directories. Refactor verified by all existing tests passing unchanged.

Summary of implemented functionality: Scaffolded SvelteKit with Vitest (80% threshold) and an envelope parser mirroring the Go envelope.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: None.
Deviations & technical decisions: npm instead of pnpm (pnpm not installed); Node >= 20.19 required by Vite 8, so a newer Node is prepended to PATH per command. 3 low-severity npm audit findings (transitive cookie) left unfixed because the suggested fix is a breaking downgrade.

Summary of implemented functionality: Built the host web flow: /auth/login (email OTP), /events/new (category picker, details, collapsed overrides), /events/[id] (short link, QR, downloads); API client with credentials, timeout, status and Retry-After; jsdom component tests; /api dev proxy.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: None for the API. The web app is now a client-side SPA (ssr off) and expects /api on its own origin (Vite proxy in dev; a reverse proxy is needed in deployment).
Deviations & technical decisions: Time zone is a read-only WIB label because POST /api/v1/events accepts none (user chose this over extending the backend). Signed-out hosts are detected by a 401 and sent to /auth/login?next=..., because there is no session-check endpoint; the typed form is lost on that bounce. Components are unit-tested with mocked API modules; the real sign-in path was not exercised end to end (no Redis/Mailpit). Review fixes: 15 s request timeout, hidden reveal delay reset, no duplicate create after a failed navigation, reload on route id change. A real-browser check found resolve.conditions: [] in vite.config.ts broke onMount in dev and build (fixed, regression test src/config.test.ts).

Summary of implemented functionality: Added Playwright end-to-end tests that drive Chrome through the Vite proxy to the real API, Postgres, Redis and Mailpit (scripts/e2e.sh), and made scripts/check.sh run them; timed the scripted host flow against the 3-minute target.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: scripts/check.sh now needs Docker (Redis + Mailpit up), Chrome and TEST_DATABASE_URL; SKIP_E2E=1 skips the e2e step with a loud notice. Port 8080 is held by an unrelated Apache service on the dev machine, so e2e uses 8081/9091/5174.
Deviations & technical decisions: Installed Chrome instead of downloading Playwright browsers; e2e uses a throwaway sela_e2e_<pid> database on the local Postgres and resets only rl:/attempts:/lock: keys on the compose Redis; one unique email per test because of the OTP rate limits; the QR PNG is decoded with jsqr to prove it encodes the short link; scripted time is a lower bound and not the PRD metric. A typescript review found no CRITICAL/HIGH; the MEDIUMs (unguarded database-URL rewrite, unchecked Redis container, one-shot QR load check) were fixed in 7b11984. Also added .gitattributes so shell scripts keep LF.

Summary of implemented functionality: Wired config, Postgres, Redis, SMTP and the auth service into one process serving HTTP and gRPC, with an end-to-end test.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: cmd/api's run() now takes (ctx, getenv); the server no longer starts without the required environment.
Deviations & technical decisions: Services stay packages in one process (deviation from separate deployables, recorded in FSD 2.6). go test -race unavailable locally (needs cgo/gcc); run it in CI.

Summary of implemented functionality: Added a CLI that applies (up) or reverts (down) migrations against DATABASE_URL.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: None.
Deviations & technical decisions: Default command is up; DSN is never printed; run() is injectable for tests.

Summary of implemented functionality: Verified the email OTP flow live against docker compose Redis and Mailpit with the real API; all checks passed without service changes.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: None.
Deviations & technical decisions: Verification lives in apps/web/tests/e2e/auth-live.spec.ts so it is repeatable; compose's postgres was not used because a local PostgreSQL 17 owns 5432.

Summary of implemented functionality: Added Docker Compose services (Postgres, Redis, Mailpit) bound to localhost with required credentials, .env.example and scripts/check.sh.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: None.
Deviations & technical decisions: Compose refuses to start without credentials; check.sh became the single validation entrypoint.

Breaking changes / structural refactors: None.
Deviations & technical decisions: PRD and BRD intentionally unchanged: implementation so far does not change product scope, and their documented inconsistencies (MVP category count, free-tier watermark, BR-17 numbering) stay open. docs/ is gitignored, so these updates are not in commits.

Summary of implemented functionality: Updated the FSD to v2.6 and this tracker for Task 4.

Deviations & technical decisions: PRD and BRD still unchanged; the fallback defaults are recorded in FSD 4.1 as derived from BRD 7/10 for product review.

Summary of implemented functionality: Updated the FSD to v2.8 (10.1 implementation note, change row, 11.1 status for FR-01.1, FR-01.2, FR-01.3, FR-09.1), CLAUDE.md and this tracker for Task 6.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: None.

Breaking changes / structural refactors: None.
Deviations & technical decisions: Milestone 1 is complete except T7.2 (human timed sessions), which stays Pending Verification. FR-09.1 stays Partial because SMS OTP is not built. docs/ tracker files are versioned; FSD/PRD/BRD .md and .pdf are still ignored.

Summary of implemented functionality: Added fail-fast environment loading with aggregated errors and redacted printing.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: The API now refuses to start without DATABASE_URL, REDIS_ADDR, SMTP_ADDR, SMTP_FROM and OTP_HMAC_KEY (>= 32 characters).
Deviations & technical decisions: Secrets never appear in errors or String(); COOKIE_SECURE defaults to true.

Summary of implemented functionality: Added the goose migration runner and migrations 0001-0003: hosts, event_categories (six seeded presets) and events.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: New database schema (three migrations). Column names are English forms of FSD 5 (batas_jepretan -> shot_limit, etc.).
Deviations & technical decisions: Undefined category defaults are stored as 'tbd', never invented. goose pinned to v3.26.0 because v3.28 requires Go 1.26 and silently raised the module's Go version. Cover image and branding columns deferred. Categories are presets, not gates. PII encryption deferred (needs a blind index for the unique lookups).

Summary of implemented functionality: Extracted the strict JSON body decoder into httpx, added the required SHORT_LINK_BASE_URL setting, extended event.proto, and added a deny-by-default gRPC host interceptor.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: SHORT_LINK_BASE_URL is now required at startup (the API refuses to start without it). event.proto changes are additive (new field numbers).
Deviations & technical decisions: The auth handlers were refactored onto httpx.DecodeJSON with the existing tests as the safety net. The interceptor reuses the auth package's HostID and error mapping instead of duplicating them.

Summary of implemented functionality: Added the shared JSON envelope {success, data, error}, a GET /healthz handler and an HTTP entrypoint with graceful shutdown.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: None.
Deviations & technical decisions: Envelope follows the project API-response rule; health checks no dependencies (liveness only).

Summary of implemented functionality: Implemented the OTP sign-in core: hashed single-use 5-minute codes, rate limits, lockout, hashed 12-hour sessions, Postgres find-or-create host and an SMTP mailer.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: Adds runtime dependencies on Redis and an SMTP relay.
Deviations & technical decisions: Code consumed before host creation so concurrent verifies cannot mis-report IsNewHost; attempts counted only while a code is outstanding to prevent lockout of addresses that never requested a code; Redis keys use keyed hashes (no raw email or IP); opaque server-side sessions instead of JWT; refresh token and logout deferred (partial FR-SEC.4).

Summary of implemented functionality: Added REST and gRPC adapters over one Flow interface, plus RequireHost middleware.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: None.
Deviations & technical decisions: HTTP handlers live in services/auth (not internal/httpx), reusing the httpx envelope. Session token only in the HttpOnly cookie (HTTP) or the response (gRPC). X-Forwarded-For deliberately ignored. Fixed generic messages for internal errors.

Summary of implemented functionality: Added the event domain: category presets with raw and effective defaults, event creation with unique short codes and private access tokens, PNG/SVG QR codes of the short link, and host-scoped retrieval.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: None to existing endpoints; new tables are read and written (events, event_categories) with no schema change.
Deviations & technical decisions: FSD does not define what a tbd default falls back to, so the fallback is unlimited shots and instant reveal, derived from BRD 7/10 and FSD 4.5. Host override beats a defined category default beats the fallback. Wedding reveal_at = start of the event day (Asia/Jakarta) + 24h, an interpretation of 'delayed 1 day' that needs product confirmation. shot_limit 0 means explicitly unlimited. reveal_delay_hours capped at 8760 (safety limit, not in the docs). Not-owner and not-found are both ErrNotFound so existence is not leaked. Timezone data is embedded (time/tzdata). Short-link resolver deliberately deferred.

Summary of implemented functionality: Added the public short-link resolver GET /e/{short_code} returning guest-safe event metadata; short links and QR codes now encode {SHORT_LINK_BASE_URL}/e/{code}.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: Short links/QR codes created before this change lack /e/ (dev/test data only).
Deviations & technical decisions: Invalid, unknown, non-active and expired codes all return one identical 404; 200 JSON rather than a redirect (no guest PWA yet); no rate limiting yet (follow-up); no proto change.

Summary of implemented functionality: Exposed the event use cases over REST and gRPC and wired them into the API process.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: cmd/api's newMux and newGRPCServer now take the event dependencies; the gRPC server always installs the host interceptor, so every method outside the public allowlist requires a Bearer session.
Deviations & technical decisions: Category listing is public (presets, not host data); everything else needs a session. The RPC keeps the name ListEventCategories (existing contract) instead of ListCategories. Responses are built from types that have no host_id or access_token field, and request bodies containing host_id are rejected. HTTP handlers live in services/event and reuse the httpx envelope. golangci-lint timeout raised to 5 minutes in check.sh.

Summary of implemented functionality: Added the rbac API client, a best-effort profile fetch in the root layout, a dynamic Nav component, a real dark theme palette, and a new /settings page with real EN/ID language and theme switching.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: The root layout's load() now returns a required profile field, which is merged into every page's PageData type (existing dashboard tests updated to pass profile: null).
Deviations & technical decisions: Only the nav and the new settings page get real i18n; the three existing host pages keep hardcoded Indonesian text (a larger, separate retrofit). A failed/401 profile fetch resolves to profile: null rather than throwing, so /auth/login never breaks. PATCH only sets concrete theme/language values, not 'clear back to inherited' (fast-follow).

Summary of implemented functionality: Verified the RBAC foundation against the real stack (Docker Redis+Mailpit, local Postgres, scripts/check.sh) and synced the FSD, CLAUDE.md and this tracker for Task 9.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: None.
Deviations & technical decisions: RBAC isn't tied to a numbered FR yet; no ID was invented (see FSD 11.1). Menu nesting and the dropdown tables are built and tested but unseeded, since no second real menu destination or dropdown consumer exists yet. Numbered this Task 9, not Task 8: the FSD (gitignored, not tracked here before now) already used 'Task 8' for a planned Milestone 2 migration (guest_sessions/media, FSD change-note v2.9→v2.10) that has no corresponding code or tracker entry yet — a pre-existing drift between the FSD and this tracker, left as discovered rather than silently reconciled. docs/ is gitignored, so these edits are not versioned in git.

Summary of implemented functionality: Implemented the RBAC foundation for real: migrations for roles/menus/dropdowns/actions/permissions, a services/rbac package (Postgres repository, Service resolving per-role menus/actions/dropdowns/preferences with a host-then-role-then-global fallback chain), GET /api/v1/auth/me and PATCH /api/v1/me/preferences, and events:create enforcement on the already-shipped POST /api/v1/events.
Breaking changes / structural refactors: POST /api/v1/events now requires the events:create permission in addition to a host session; every existing host is granted it by default in the seed, so behavior is unchanged unless a permission is explicitly revoked.
Deviations & technical decisions: Fallback-chain and ancestor-inclusion logic lives in Go (table-driven tested), not PL/pgSQL, matching this codebase's zero-stored-procedure convention; the one exception is a menu cycle-prevention trigger, a genuine data-integrity invariant a CHECK can't express. Seed data stays minimal and real: 2 flat menus (events_new, settings), 2 enforced permissions (events:create, profile:update); dropdowns and nested menus are schema-complete and tested but unseeded, since no real consumer exists yet. REST only, no gRPC, for /auth/me (fast-follow, mirrors Task 5's precedent). No permission-check caching (single API instance).
